subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Is the July 3 session-stable binding work sufficient to close this OpenAI prompt-cache churn report, or should maintainers require a fresh current-main live cache trace first?
rationale: Source shows partial stabilization but not enough to prove the original OpenAI/WhatsApp cold-turn symptom is gone, and the remaining fix shape can affect visible-reply guidance.

options.title: Require current-main live proof
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a live OpenAI cache trace across normal, room-event, and subagent completion turns before closing or queueing repair.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow prompt-cache repair
options.body: If live proof still shows churn, choose a maintainer-owned fix shape that keeps visible-reply safety while moving or stabilizing volatile delivery guidance.

options.title: Accept main-only mitigation
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide the session-stable binding commits are sufficient despite no fresh live OpenAI measurement on this report.

recommendation.title: Require current-main live proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a live OpenAI cache trace across normal, room-event, and subagent completion turns before closing or queueing repair.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the closest current-main changes to session-stable prompt and tool-scope binding facts.
